title: A 0.52mJ/Frame 107fps Super-Resolution Processor Exploiting Pseudo-FP6 Sparsity for Mobile Applications
problem: CNN-based super-resolution (SRCNN) for mobile applications suffers from three challenges: (1) large on-chip memory for multi-dimensional overlapping regions in layer-fusion limits external-bandwidth reduction, (2) traditional low-bit-width quantization degrades image quality, requiring novel high-dynamic-range computation, (3) deconvolution accounts for large workload but reusing convolution datapath creates redundant calculations.
method: Mobile super-resolution processor using pseudo-FP6 (low-bit-width high-dynamic-range) quantization, memory-optimized layer-fusion dataflow minimizing overlapping-region buffering, and efficient deconvolution processing, achieving 0.52mJ/frame at 107fps.

title: Delving into Topology Representation for Layout Pattern: A Novel Contrastive Learning Framework for Hotspot Detection
problem: Machine learning-based layout hotspot detection struggles to capture decision boundaries across entire datasets and ignores geometric/topological properties of polygons.
method: CLI-HD: contrastive learning framework operating on layout sequences and images; Layout2Seq encodes polygon shapes as vectors within sequences; absolute position embedding replaces standard Transformer positional encodings to capture topology.

title: TNIC: A Trusted NIC Architecture: A hardware-network substrate for building high-performance trustworthy distributed systems
problem: Distributed systems deployed in heterogeneous cloud environments face Byzantine failures from untrusted hardware and software, but existing trusted execution environments (TEEs) are CPU-centric and incur high performance overhead when attempting to enforce network-level trust guarantees such as non-equivocation and transferable authentication.
method: TNIC builds a minimal, formally verified silicon root-of-trust at the NIC level using SmartNIC hardware. It provides two core cryptographic primitives—transferable authentication (signed message delivery) and non-equivocation (monotonic counters preventing double-send attacks)—implemented in hardware-accelerated network processing logic. The TCB is minimized by placing trust enforcement at the network interface, making it CPU-agnostic. TNIC exposes programming APIs and a recipe for constructing Byzantine-fault-tolerant distributed protocols, demonstrated via four trustworthy distributed systems built on the substrate.

title: 1.78mJ/Frame 373fps 3D GS Processor Based on Shape-Aware Hybrid Architecture Using Earlier Computation Skipping and Gaussian Cache Scheduler
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D GS) rendering on edge devices suffers from variable Gaussian distribution shapes requiring complex projection+rasterization dataflow, diverse input-dependent inefficient computations, and irregular memory access patterns for millions of spherical-harmonic coefficients.
method: The processor employs a shape-aware hybrid architecture that detects and skips redundant computations based on Gaussian properties, uses early computation termination when results become insignificant, and implements a smart Gaussian cache scheduler to reduce irregular off-chip memory traffic for SH coefficients.

title: 27.4 A BJT-Based Temperature Sensor with an 80fJ.K2 Resolution FoM
problem: BJT-based temperature sensors require high energy efficiency while maintaining high accuracy; existing designs using resistor-based sensors or CT-ΔΣM approaches consume more power or occupy larger area.
method: NPN-based temperature sensor using noise-optimized charge-balancing continuous-time ΔΣ modulator (CTΔΣM) to digitize PTAT and CTAT current ratio. Current-assisted amplifier improves conversion gain while maintaining low noise.

title: A Dynamically Reconfigurable Digital-Integrated Voltage-Regulator Fabric for Energy-Efficient DVFS in Multi-Domain soCs
problem: Conventional SoC voltage-regulator (VR) architectures use static domain grouping and fixed buck topologies determined at design time. However, SoC domains continuously undergo power-state transitions with changing voltage and current loads; static groupings cannot dynamically reconfigure to maximize efficiency, precluding runtime voltage scaling optimizations.
method: A reconfigurable digital-integrated voltage-regulator fabric enables runtime VR reconfiguration. The fabric allows: (1) dynamic domain regrouping to reflect changing power states, (2) multi-phase buck converter disaggregation when high current compliance is unnecessary, (3) dynamic LDO reassignment to minimize dropout losses. Runtime reconfiguration exploits current operating conditions to maximize aggregate VR efficiency.

title: Late Breaking Results: A Diffusion-Based Framework for Configurable and Realistic Multi-Storage Trace Generation
problem: Existing storage trace generation methods lack the ability to produce realistic, configurable, and diverse multi-device traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies with high fidelity.
method: DiTTO uses diffusion models to synthesize high-fidelity continuous traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies. The framework allows user-defined configurations while maintaining fidelity to real storage patterns, achieving trace generation with only 8% configuration errors.

title: Snowplow: Effective Kernel Fuzzing with a Learned White-box Test Mutator
problem: Kernel fuzzers rely on program mutation to generate test programs that explore new kernel code paths, but existing mutation heuristics are unable to navigate the complex control and data flow of kernel code to produce mutations that trigger target code locations or increase coverage, resulting in low fuzzing effectiveness.
method: Snowplow uses a learned white-box test mutator that employs machine learning to guide mutation decisions based on kernel code analysis (control flow graphs and data flow) rather than purely random or hand-coded heuristics. The model is trained to predict which system call insertions, argument value changes, or structural mutations are most likely to move execution toward uncovered or target code regions. The white-box analysis of kernel source provides the coverage feedback signal used during training and inference.

title: TempGraph: An Efficient Chain-driven Temporal Graph Computing Framework on the GPU
problem: Temporal graph path problems require vertices to be processed sequentially along time-dependent chains, creating inherently poor parallelism and slow convergence that prevents existing GPU solutions from utilizing the massive thread-level parallelism and high memory bandwidth of modern GPUs.
method: TempGraph transforms the temporal graph into disjoint time-dependent chains that expose temporal dependencies explicitly, then employs a Generate-Activate-Compute (GAC) execution model to decouple temporal dependencies between different chains by maintaining a set of shortcut references. This allows multiple chains to be processed concurrently by massive GPU thread pools while shortcut maintenance handles cross-chain dependency resolution, enabling fast convergence and high parallelism.

title: Specialized IC for World-Lock Rendering in Augmented and Mixed Reality Devices
problem: AR/MR requires real-time rendering of virtual objects locked to the physical world, demanding high-frequency pose tracking and low-latency graphics; this cannot be done efficiently on mobile CPUs.
method: The IC combines specialized vision (camera ISP, optical flow) and graphics engines optimized for tracking and rendering. It integrates pose estimation, world reconstruction, and graphics pipeline in silicon.

title: Squeezing Operator Performance Potential for the Ascend Architecture
problem: Huawei's Ascend domain-specific architecture requires manual management of memory operations and operator execution, creating complex performance bottlenecks that are difficult to diagnose with existing roofline models. Existing roofline models suffer from visualization complexity and inaccurate performance assessment when applied to Ascend's component-level architecture.
method: The paper introduces a component-based roofline model that abstracts individual hardware components (compute units, memory subsystems, data pipelines) to capture per-component performance ceilings and identify bottleneck components. This model is combined with a structured optimization process derived from practical operator optimization case studies on Ascend, identifying common performance issues (e.g., memory bandwidth saturation, pipeline bubbles) and their targeted optimization strategies.

title: Late Breaking Results: Novel Design of MTJ-Based Unified LIF Spiking Neuron and PUF
problem: SNNs offer superior energy and hardware efficiency over DNNs but lack effective security mechanisms; integrating security with neuromorphic computing requires both functional neuromorphic circuits and cryptographic key generation.
method: Proposes an MTJ-based LIF (Leaky Integrate-and-Fire) neuron that simultaneously functions as both a spiking neuron and physically unclonable function (PUF). The design leverages MTJ's magnetic properties for dual-mode operation through unified circuit architecture.

title: 3.2 A 36V Current-Balancing Instrumentation Amplifier with ±24V Input Range, 5.6MHz BW, and 140dB CMRR at All Gain Settings
problem: Industrial instrumentation amplifiers must handle large differential input ranges (>20V) with large common-mode input offsets (±10V), require high CMRR (>120dB), high input impedance (>10MΩ), and wide bandwidth while processing millivolt-level signals from sensors.
method: 36V high-voltage instrumentation amplifier with current-balancing architecture enabling ±24V differential input range and ±10V CM input handling. Direct coupling with carefully designed gain stages maintains 140dB CMRR across all gain settings.

title: NOVA: A Novel Vertex Management Architecture for Scalable Graph Processing
problem: Existing graph processing hardware accelerators require temporal graph partitioning to fit the working set into on-chip memory, limiting scalability to large graphs and causing bandwidth inefficiency from repeated DRAM accesses across partition sweeps.
method: NOVA decouples reduction and propagation operations in the vertex-centric graph processing paradigm, allowing the entire working set to reside in off-chip DRAM rather than being partitioned across on-chip memory. On-chip memory is repurposed as a prefetch/access buffer to hide DRAM latency rather than as a traditional cache holding graph state. The design enables spatial tiling across multiple NOVA nodes for scale-out, achieving near-perfect weak and strong scaling. A cycle-accurate gem5-based model validates the architecture.

title: Concurrency-Informed Orchestration for Serverless Functions
problem: Serverless FaaS platforms suffer excessive cold starts because existing container keep-alive policies ignore concurrent invocations: they fail to reason about whether reusing a busy container (delayed warm start) or cold-starting a new container is preferable, and they make imbalanced eviction decisions that prematurely evict soon-to-be-reused containers.
method: CIDRE is a container orchestration algorithm that combines fine-grained container-level state (busy/idle, time-to-free) with coarse-grained concurrency signals to speculatively decide between a delayed warm start and a cold start under concurrent scaling. For eviction, CIDRE uses both container-level recency and concurrency-aware reuse probability to produce balanced eviction decisions that avoid removing containers still likely to be reused. The algorithm is evaluated on two production FaaS workload traces.

title: EFFACT: A Highly Efficient Full-Stack FHE Acceleration Platform
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) suffers from massive ciphertext expansion (thousands of times over plaintext) and enormous off-chip memory bandwidth demands during bootstrapping and privacy-preserving ML inference, making it impractically slow on existing hardware.
method: EFFACT combines a compiler with comprehensive optimizations and vector-friendly hardware targeting both FPGA and ASIC. Key mechanisms include: (1) a streaming memory access scheme that achieves high throughput with limited on-chip SRAM by overlapping data movement with computation; (2) a circuit-level function unit reuse scheme that reduces computing resources without performance loss; (3) novel NTT (Number Theoretic Transform) and automorphism hardware units designed for cost-sensitive architectures. An ISA and compiler backend support multiple FHE schemes (CKKS, BGV, BFV), and design space exploration determines optimal SRAM sizing.
